en: to be recruited; to be collected

examples.en: Participants are recruited this week.
A hundred volunteers were recruited.
I'll contact you as soon as staff are recruited.

examples.ko: 학생이 충분히 모집되지 않아서 수업이 취소됐어요.
examples.en: The class was canceled because not enough students signed up.
The people who were recruited will gather next week.
New members will soon be recruited.

explain: '모집되다'는 사람을 구하는 일이 진행되어 사람들이 모였을 때 써요. 구하는 쪽은 '모집하다'를 써요. 공고에서는 '모집 중'이나 '모집 마감'처럼 짧게 자주 써요.

phrases.en: We are recruiting volunteers now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공고에서 자주 보는 짧은 말로, 지금 사람을 구하고 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short phrase often seen in notices, meaning recruitment is in progress.

phrases.en: Today is the recruitment deadline.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 구하는 일이 끝나는 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to when recruitment ends.

phrases.en: The people have not all been recruited yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 사람이 덜 모였다는 뜻의 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning not enough people have gathered yet.

explain_en: 모집되다 is used when a drive to find people has progressed and people have been gathered. The side doing the recruiting uses 모집하다. In notices you often see the short forms 모집 중 (now recruiting) and 모집 마감 (recruitment closed).

dis.h: called for or gathered, like members

p.n: 채용되다 means actually hired; 모집되다 means applicants are being sought.

t90.ax: New members will soon be recruited.

en: to be sent; to be forwarded

examples.en: The book I ordered was shipped yesterday.
The email is sent automatically at the set time.
The invitations were sent out to all the guests.
I will let you know by text when the item is shipped.

examples.ko: 아직 발송되지 않은 편지가 책상에 있어요.
examples.en: There is a letter on the desk that has not been sent yet.

examples.ko: 발송된 소포는 이틀 뒤에 도착할 거예요.
examples.en: The parcel that was sent will arrive in two days.

explain: 발송되다는 쇼핑몰 문자나 회사 안내에서 자주 보는 '보내졌다'의 공식적인 말이에요. 주어는 물건·메일·서류예요. 내가 보낼 때는 '보내다'를 쓰고, 회사가 보낼 때 '발송하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The item is scheduled to be sent tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쇼핑몰이 보낼 날을 알려 줄 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when a shop announces the shipping date.

phrases.en: The letter was sent today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday word for the same idea.

phrases.en: The text message hasn't been sent yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 보내지지 않았다는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form: not sent yet.

explain_en: 발송되다 is the formal 'has been sent' that you see in shopping-site texts and company notices; the subject is an item, mail or document. When you send something yourself you say '보내다'; a company says '발송하다'.

t90.ax: The book I ordered was shipped yesterday.

examples.en: This magazine is published every month.

examples.ko: 새 책이 다음 주에 발행될 거예요.
examples.en: The new book will be published next week.

examples.ko: 표는 결제한 뒤에 바로 발행되고 있어요.
examples.en: Tickets are issued right after payment.
I read a newspaper that was published long ago.
So far one million copies have been printed.

examples.ko: 기념 우표가 발행되면 우체국에 줄이 길어요.
examples.en: When a commemorative stamp is issued, the line at the post office gets long.

explain: 책, 신문, 잡지, 영수증, 표, 우표 모두 '발행되다'와 쓸 수 있어요. 책은 '출판되다', '출간되다'도 쓰는데, 영수증이나 표처럼 만들어 내주는 것에는 '발행되다'가 어울려요.

phrases.en: A receipt is issued when you pay.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만들어서 내주는 서류나 표에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits documents or tickets that are made and handed out.

phrases.example: 새 우표가 다음 달에 새로 발행돼요.
phrases.en: A new stamp will be issued next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새로'를 붙여 처음 만들어 내놓는다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '새로' means it is newly put out.

phrases.en: The ticket hasn't been issued yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 만들어서 내주지 않았다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning it has not yet been issued.

explain_en: Books, newspapers, magazines, receipts, tickets, and stamps can all be '발행되다'. Books also use '출판되다' and '출간되다', but for things that are produced and handed out, like receipts and tickets, '발행되다' fits.

gh: a book gets printed and released
a book comes out; common in publisher news

p.n: 출판되다 is for books or printed works, not stamps.

t90.ax: This magazine is published every month.

en: to be distributed; to be released; to be circulated

examples.en: The notice was handed out to all students.
The new version will be released tomorrow.
Masks are being handed out for free.
I'll tell you by email once the materials are out.
A wrong file got released, and now we're in trouble.
Please update the released app now.

explain: 배포하다의 피동이에요. 누가 나눠 줬는지보다 나눠졌다는 사실이 중요할 때 써요. 공지, 뉴스, 앱 업데이트 소식에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: This book is distributed for free at the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배포되다'와 함께 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말 중 하나로, 값 없이 나눠진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very common pairing, meaning something is handed out at no cost.

phrases.example: 새 앱은 다음 주에 배포될 예정이에요.
phrases.en: The new app is scheduled to be released next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 나올 일을 알릴 때 쓰는 미래 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A future expression used to announce something upcoming.

phrases.en: That video was widely circulated on the internet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자료나 영상이 온라인으로 퍼질 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when materials or videos spread online.

explain_en: This is the passive of '배포하다'. Use it when the fact that something went out matters more than who sent it. It shows up often in notices, news, and app update announcements.

t90.ax: Please update the released app now.

en: meeting to launch the New Year

examples.ko: 연초 시무식에는 임직원이 모두 대강당에 모여요.
examples.en: At the New Year launch ceremony, all the staff gather in the main hall.
This year's opening ceremony is held on the morning of January 2.
At the opening ceremony, the CEO announced this year's goals.
Our company keeps the New Year opening ceremony simple.
After the opening ceremony, I ate rice cake soup with my teammates.

examples.ko: 시무식 때 입을 정장을 미리 챙겨 놓았어요.
examples.en: I got my suit ready in advance for the opening ceremony.

explain: 회사나 기관에서 새해 첫 출근일에 하는 행사예요. 반대로 한 해를 마무리하는 행사는 '종무식'이라고 해요. '시무식을 하다', '시무식을 열다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The company holds its New Year opening ceremony on January 2 every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새해 첫 출근일에 행사를 한다는 가장 기본적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for holding the first-day-of-work event.

phrases.en: All employees attended the opening ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사에 직접 가서 함께할 때 '참석하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 참석하다 is used for attending in person.

phrases.en: At the end of December, we hold a year-end ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시무식과 반대로 한 해의 마지막 날에 하는 행사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 시무식, held at the end of the year.

explain_en: This is the event a company or organization holds on the first working day of the new year. The event that wraps up the year is called '종무식'. You say '시무식을 하다' or '시무식을 열다'.

en: to be requested; to be asked for

examples.en: Submission of this document is requested by tomorrow.
If help is requested, I'll go right away.
Attendance at the meeting was requested.
It's a situation where cooperation is requested.
Additional materials may be requested.

examples.ko: 요청된 일은 오늘 안에 끝내야 해요.
examples.en: The requested work has to be finished today.

explain: '~이/가 요청되다'는 주어가 요청받는 일이라서 누가 요청했는지는 말하지 않아요. 안내문, 공문, 뉴스에서 자주 보이고 일상 대화에서는 '부탁받다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: My friend asked me to help with moving.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '요청되다' 대신 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in daily talk instead of 요청되다.

phrases.en: I asked a staff member for help.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 직접 부탁하는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, where a person asks directly.

phrases.en: That material has not been requested yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 부탁받지 않았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it hasn't been asked for yet.

explain_en: The subject is the thing being asked for, and who asked is left unsaid. You see it in notices, official letters, and news. In everyday talk people prefer simpler phrasing such as 부탁받다.

dis.h: be asked for politely; formally requested
gh: be required as a necessity; demanded

p.n: 요구되다 makes it sound like a demand or requirement, not a polite request.

examples.en: The president is in his office right now.
I waited for a moment in front of the office door.
The mayor's office is on the third floor.
The office was full of a big desk and papers.
When guests come, we talk in the office.
The president's office appeared on the news.

explain: 집무실은 높은 직책의 사람이 일하는 방이에요. 일반 직원의 일하는 곳은 '사무실'이라고 하고, 사장이나 시장처럼 책임이 큰 사람의 방일 때 집무실이라고 해요. 보통 '대통령 집무실', '사장 집무실'처럼 직책과 함께 말해요.

phrases.en: The president's office is in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집무실과 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with 집무실.

phrases.en: The secretary went into the office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방에 들어가는 움직임을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the action of entering the room.

phrases.en: The mayor moved his office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 방을 다른 곳으로 바꿀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when changing the room where one works to another place.

explain_en: 집무실 is the room where a high-ranking person works. A regular employee's workplace is a 사무실, while 집무실 is used for the room of someone with big responsibility, like a president or mayor. It usually comes with a title, as in 대통령 집무실 or 사장 집무실.

t90.ax: When guests come, we talk in the office.

en: first issue; launch of a publication

examples.ko: 이 잡지는 올해 창간 오십 주년을 맞았어요.
examples.en: This magazine marks the fiftieth anniversary of its launch this year.

examples.ko: 신문사는 창간 기념 행사를 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: The newspaper company is preparing an event to celebrate its founding.
The first issue sold out in a few days.

examples.ko: 그 잡지의 창간 멤버들이 오랜만에 모였어요.
examples.en: The founding members of the magazine got together for the first time in a long while.

examples.ko: 창간 때부터 이 칼럼을 읽어 왔어요.
examples.en: I have been reading this column since the very first issue.

examples.ko: 창간 준비 중인 웹진에서 글을 부탁했어요.
examples.en: A webzine that is getting ready to launch asked me to write something.

explain: 창간은 신문이나 잡지를 처음 낼 때 써요. 방송이 처음 시작할 때는 '개국', 가게는 '개업'처럼 분야마다 말이 달라요. 반대로 신문이나 잡지를 아예 접을 때는 '폐간'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I still have the first issue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신문이나 잡지의 맨 처음 호를 말해요. 수집하는 사람이 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The very first issue of a newspaper or magazine, which many people collect.

phrases.en: Today is the newspaper's founding anniversary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신문이나 잡지를 처음 낸 날을 기념하는 날이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The day that marks when the paper or magazine first came out.

phrases.en: I'm busy preparing to launch a new magazine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 내기 전에 기획하고 만드는 단계를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The planning and making stage before the first issue comes out.

explain_en: This word is only for the very first issue of a newspaper or magazine. Other fields have their own words: a broadcaster starting up is '개국' and a shop opening is '개업'. Shutting a publication down for good is '폐간'.

t90.ax: The first issue sold out in a few days.

examples.en: A new menu item was added.
The name wasn't added to the list.
If you order, a shipping fee is added.
A new feature will be added to the app.
I marked the added content in yellow.
One more assignment got added, so it's tough.

explain: 이미 있는 것에 더해진다는 말이에요. 반대로 빠지는 것은 '삭제되다', '제외되다'를 써요. 직접 더할 때는 '추가하다'예요. 돈이 더 붙을 때는 '비용이 추가되다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The newly added menu item is really tasty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 더해진 것을 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for something newly added.

phrases.example: 다음 달에 새 기능이 추가될 거예요.
phrases.en: A new feature will be added next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 더해질 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that will be added in the future.

phrases.en: I had many bags, so extra cost was added.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 더 붙을 때 쓰는 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for extra charges.

explain_en: It means something is added on top of what already exists. The opposite, for things taken out, is '삭제되다' or '제외되다'. When you add something yourself, use '추가하다'. Extra costs are also described with this verb: '비용이 추가되다'.

t90.ax: A new menu item was added.

examples.ko: 오래된 집이라 배관이 낡아서 물이 샐 때가 있어요.
examples.en: It's an old house, so the pipes are worn and sometimes leak.

examples.ko: 욕실 배관을 새로 바꾸는 데 이틀 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Replacing the bathroom plumbing took two days.

examples.ko: 배관 공사 때문에 오늘 아침에 물이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: The water didn't come on this morning because of the plumbing work.
I called a plumber and he fixed it right away.

examples.ko: 벽 안쪽 배관은 눈에 보이지 않아서 점검이 어려워요.
examples.en: The pipes inside the wall can't be seen, so inspecting them is hard.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 배관이 얼지 않게 보온재를 감아 두세요.
examples.en: In winter, wrap the pipes with insulation so they don't freeze.

explain: 물, 가스, 난방용으로 설치한 관 전체를 말해요. 관 하나하나는 '파이프'나 '관'이라고 해요. 수리하는 사람은 '배관공'이고, 집에서 물이 샐 때 '배관 공사'를 한다고 말해요.

phrases.en: The pipes are clogged, so the water will not drain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이나 쓰레기 때문에 관이 막혔을 때 쓰는 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common expression for when pipes are blocked by water or trash.

phrases.en: A plumber came and fixed the water pipe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배관을 설치하고 고치는 일을 하는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person whose job is installing and repairing pipes.

phrases.en: I replaced the rusty pipe with a new one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배관'은 관 전체를 말하고, '파이프'는 관 하나하나를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 배관 means the whole piping system, while 파이프 means each individual pipe.

explain_en: It refers to the whole system of pipes installed for water, gas or heating. A single pipe is called '파이프' or '관'. The repair worker is a '배관공', and when a house leaks you say you do '배관 공사' (plumbing work).

examples.en: The library keeps guide booklets at the entrance.
They placed a fire extinguisher in each room.
The hotel room is provided with an umbrella.

examples.ko: 응급 약품을 비치한 곳을 알아 두세요.
examples.en: Know where the emergency medicine is kept.
There are many items to put out, so organizing is needed.
It's convenient to keep water in the car.

explain: 필요할 때 쓰도록 건물이나 방에 물건을 미리 갖춰 두는 것이에요. 공공시설, 호텔, 병원 안내문에서 많이 봐요. 일상에서는 '두다'나 '준비해 놓다'가 더 자연스러워요. '비치되어 있어요'로도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: A fire extinguisher is provided on each floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 공공 장소에서 가장 많이 보는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form you most often see on notices and in public places.

phrases.en: We put a first aid kit in the office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요할 때 쓰도록 미리 두는 물건과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with items kept ready in advance for when they are needed.
phrases.en_equiv: to keep a first aid kit ready

phrases.en: We kept umbrellas ready for our guests.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비치하다'보다 일상적으로 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word you can use more casually than '비치하다'.

explain_en: It means placing items in advance in a building or room so they can be used when needed. You see it on notices in public facilities, hotels, and hospitals. In daily speech 두다 or 준비해 놓다 is more natural. '비치되어 있어요' is also common.

t90.ax: It's convenient to keep water in the car.

examples.ko: 이 호텔은 최신 시설을 완비하고 있어요.
examples.en: This hotel is fully equipped with the latest facilities.

examples.ko: 새 도서관은 조용한 공부 공간을 완비했어요.
examples.en: The new library has fully set up quiet study spaces.

examples.ko: 학교가 안전 장치를 완비해야 학부모들이 안심해요.
examples.en: Parents feel at ease only when the school has all safety measures in place.
I completed all the required documents and submitted them.

examples.ko: 주방 시설을 완비한 원룸을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a studio apartment with a fully equipped kitchen.

examples.ko: 병원이 응급 장비를 완비하면 더 많은 환자를 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the hospital fully equips its emergency gear, it can take more patients.

explain: 시설, 장비, 서류가 빠짐없이 다 갖춰졌다는 뜻이라서 호텔이나 부동산 광고에서 '시설 완비'처럼 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '다 갖추다'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 이 기숙사는 샤워실과 세탁실을 완비하고 있어요.
phrases.en: This dormitory is fully equipped with a shower room and a laundry room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시설'과 함께 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말로, 광고에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common pairing with 시설 and is often seen in advertisements.
phrases.en_equiv: to be fully equipped with facilities

phrases.en: Every room has heating and cooling fully provided.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완비하다'의 피동 형태로, 시설이나 장비가 이미 다 갖춰진 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the passive form of 완비하다 and describes facilities or equipment being already fully in place.

phrases.example: 필요한 물건을 다 갖추고 여행을 떠났어요.
phrases.en: I got everything I needed together and left on the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완비하다'와 같은 뜻을 일상에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the everyday way to say the same thing as 완비하다.

explain_en: It means facilities, equipment or documents are all in place with nothing missing, so you often see it in hotel or real-estate ads as '시설 완비'. In everyday conversation people usually say '다 갖추다' instead.

examples.ko: 부엌 벽에 통풍구가 있어서 환기가 잘돼요.
examples.en: There's a vent on the kitchen wall, so the air circulates well.

examples.ko: 통풍구를 막으면 방 안 공기가 탁해져요.
examples.en: If you block the vent, the air in the room gets stuffy.
A lot of dust has built up in the shoe cabinet's vent.
The new car has air vents in the back seat too.

examples.ko: 통풍구로 찬 바람이 들어와서 너무 추워요.
examples.en: Cold wind comes in through the vent, so it's very cold.
If the laptop's vent gets blocked, it heats up quickly.

explain: 벽, 차, 신발장, 노트북처럼 공기가 드나드는 구멍에 두루 써요. '통풍이 잘되다/안 되다'와 같이 기억하면 쉬워요. 막히면 열이 차거나 냄새가 날 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I cleaned the air conditioner vent on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼지가 쌓이기 쉬워서 청소하는 일이 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Dust builds up easily, so people often clean it.

phrases.en: These shoes have good airflow, so they feel cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공기가 잘 통한다는 뜻으로 함께 외우면 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means air flows well, and it is useful to learn together.

phrases.example: 노트북 통풍구가 막혀서 열이 많이 나요.
phrases.en: The laptop vent is blocked, so it gets very hot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통풍구에 먼지가 쌓이거나 물건이 있어 공기가 안 통할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when dust or objects stop air from passing through.

explain_en: It is used broadly for openings where air moves, such as in walls, cars, shoe cabinets and laptops. It is easy to remember together with '통풍이 잘되다/안 되다'. If it is blocked, heat or smell can build up.

en: plaque; hanging name board (of a building)

examples.ko: 절 입구에 오래된 현판이 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: An old name board hangs at the entrance of the temple.
The lettering on the plaque was beautiful, so I took a photo.

examples.ko: 새 건물에 현판을 다는 행사가 열려요.
examples.en: A ceremony for hanging the plaque on the new building will be held.

examples.ko: 한옥 대문 위의 현판에는 집 이름이 쓰여 있어요.
examples.en: The name of the house is written on the board above the gate of the hanok.
The school's name board fell in the wind.

examples.ko: 이 현판은 유명한 서예가가 쓴 거예요.
examples.en: A famous calligrapher wrote this plaque.

explain: 가게 이름을 단 판은 '간판'이고, 한옥, 절, 궁궐, 학교 같은 곳에 건물 이름을 써서 거는 판은 '현판'이에요. 전통 건물이나 공식 기관에 어울리는 말이에요. 새 기관이 문을 열 때 현판을 거는 행사를 '현판식'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: We hung a new name board at the entrance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물 이름을 써서 다는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means hanging a board with the building's name.

phrases.en: The library's plaque ceremony is tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 기관이 문을 열 때 현판을 거는 행사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The event when a plaque is hung for a newly opened institution.

phrases.en: We take down the old plaque and keep it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걸어 둔 현판을 내릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when taking down a hung plaque.

explain_en: A board with a shop's name is a 간판, while the board with a building's name hung on a hanok, temple, palace or school is a 현판. It suits traditional buildings and official institutions. The ceremony of hanging one when a new institution opens is called 현판식.
